applicable_when: The kernel performs a large GEMM (M=65536, N=3072, K=768) using scalar FP32 FFMA instructions because ALLOW_TF32=False. On the H200 SXM5, FP32 FFMA peaks at 67 TFLOPS while FP32 Tensor Cores (TF32) peak at 989 TFLOPS — a ~14.8x hardware advantage. The kernel currently achieves only 37% of FP32 FFMA peak (~25 TFLOPS effective), leaving enormous headroom. Enabling TF32 routes tl.dot through the Tensor Core MMA pipeline, which also reduces register pressure from the scalar accumulation loop, potentially improving the catastrophically low 12.5% occupancy (currently register-limited to 2 blocks/SM with 255 registers/thread). K=768 is moderate and the diversity instruction explicitly endorses TF32 for this kernel.

applicable_when: The kernel uses 255 registers per thread — the hardware maximum — which limits the SM to only 2 active blocks and 8 warps total (12.5% theoretical occupancy). With only 2 active warps per scheduler and 58% of cycles having no eligible warp, the GPU is severely latency-exposed. The root cause is the large BLOCK_M×BLOCK_N accumulator (128×128 fp32 = 65536 bytes of register state) combined with complex index arithmetic in the K-loop across 24 iterations (K=768/BLOCK_K=32). Increasing BLOCK_K reduces loop iterations and the associated loop-carried register state. Reducing BLOCK_M or BLOCK_N shrinks the accumulator. Adding @triton.autotune lets the runtime find the optimal tile shape for this H200.
